# CANIS-EVAL-001 — CE-09: Discriminant-Direction Seed Rebuild (all 7 axes, 3 models)

**WP2 CE-09 | Agent: Clau | Generated by `eval/ce09_discriminant_seeds.py`**

## What this is

CE-08 found the epistemic cluster (confident/uncertain/curious/concern) near-collinear in
J-space (seed-phrase cosine 0.97–0.99), so uncertain/curious/concern under-fired and
confident over-fired (65% FP on Qwen). CE-07 showed the **discriminant direction**
μ_pos − μ_neg rescues a collapsed axis (mischief 0%→76–100%). CE-09 applies that idea
**uniformly to all 7 axes, across all 3 models**, using only data already captured
(J @ h_tap for the 350 positives + 350 matched negatives per model). No model inference,
no new elicitation.

**Rigor upgrade over CE-07:** CE-07 built the seed on all positives and scored the *same*
positives (in-sample, optimistic). CE-09 uses **5-fold cross-validation** — seeds are built
on train folds and scored on held-out items — so every recall/FP number below is honest
**out-of-sample**. Classifier = argmax cosine over the 7 non-idle seeds (= CE-08 arm1 style).

**Pipeline validated:** the naive-seed baseline reproduces CE-08 arm1 recall exactly for
confident (92%), uncertain (26%), curious (72%), concern (2%) on Qwen — confirming the
re-scoring matches production before any rebuild.

**Blend:** seed(w) = normalize(w·μ_pos + (1−w)·normalize(μ_pos − μ_neg)). w=1 → pure
centroid; w=0 → pure discriminant. Non-destructive: writes `seed_vectors_<model>_ce09.npz`;
production seeds untouched.

## Headline — macro recall / FP (5-fold CV, out-of-sample)

| Model | naive seeds | w=1 centroid | w=0.5 blend | **w=0 discriminant** |
|-------|-------------|--------------|-------------|----------------------|
| Apertus-4B | 33% / 21% | 99% / 28% | 94% / 11% | **89% / 7%** |
| Ministral-3B | 27% / 18% | 99% / 24% | 99% / 16% | **95% / 9%** |
| Qwen3-4B | 55% / 21% | 98% / 22% | 94% / 9% | **92% / 6%** |

The **discriminant (w=0)** is the recommended operating point: it keeps ~90–95% recall while
**cutting FP to 6–9%** (vs 18–21% naive and 22–28% for the recall-greedy centroid). It is the
"baseline subtraction" CE-08 asked for — subtracting μ_neg removes the common-mode coalition.

(n = 50 positives / 50 matched-negatives per class; Wilson 95% CIs in `ce09_results.json`.)

## Three findings

**1. "Ministral is a weak model for J-space" was a seed artifact, not a model limitation.**
Naive Ministral was 27% macro (five of seven axes at literal 0%). With discriminant seeds it
reaches **95% macro**. The signal was always in Ministral's J-space; the hand-written seed
phrases simply didn't align with its representation. This overturns the CE-08 cross-model
ranking (Qwen > Apertus ≫ Ministral) — **all three models carry the disposition signal
strongly (89–95% CV macro recall once seeds are built from data).**

**2. The epistemic cluster separates.** curious (0% on Apertus, 2% concern on Qwen) now hits
90–100% everywhere. Seed-vector de-correlation confirms it structurally on the models where
the readout was collinear: Apertus confident↔uncertain cosine **0.940 → 0.179**, Ministral
**0.748 → −0.135**. (On Qwen the *vectors* stay collinear — 0.99 → 0.97 — yet the classifier
still separates at 94–100%, because the discriminating information lives in a small residual
subspace that argmax exploits. High cosine ≠ inseparable.)

**3. CE-07's isolated mischief rebuild silently regressed `warm`.** Scored against the
*current* production npz, naive warm on Qwen is **22%**, not the 100% CE-08 reported from the
original run — CE-07's mischief vector (rebuilt against fixed other seeds) now cannibalises
warm positives. CE-09's **joint** rebuild restores warm to 92–98%. **Lesson: rebuild all axes
together, never one at a time.** (Same cause: naive Ministral mischief over-fires at 96% FP.)

## Recommendation & honest caveats

**Deploy the w=0 discriminant seeds** (best FP at ~90%+ recall) — regenerate the npz with a
fixed `w=0` and load into the server; inference stays **forward-only and on-device** (only the
reference vectors change). Keeps **7 states** on all three models.

Caveats, stated plainly:
- **This is a *supervised* probe.** The discriminant needs ~50 labelled positives + 50 matched
  negatives per class per model to build (a one-time offline calibration). The naive
  seed-phrase readout needs no labelled data. CE-09 proves the disposition signal is *linearly
  decodable* from J-space across models; it does **not** claim zero-shot seed phrases suffice.
  The product implication: ship a small per-model calibration set, not just authored phrases.
- **Small n → wide CIs** (50/class). Treat single-class numbers as indicative.
- **Two hard axes remain:** `confident` FP stays elevated (26–38%) — consistent with the SAE
  "broad certainty coalition" finding, genuinely hard to suppress — and `curious` carries
  10–16% FP on the larger models. `mischief` recall drops at w=0 (62–94%) in exchange for its
  FP collapsing from 40–96% to 2–10%; for a safety axis that trade favours low FP.
- **w is a real knob:** w=1 maximises recall but nearly triples FP. We recommend w=0; w=0.5 is
  a middle option. We did *not* tune w to maximise the test metric beyond these three points.

## What it means for the disposition paper

The forward-only J-space readout, with reference vectors built from data via a discriminant
direction, decodes 7 disposition axes at **89–95% cross-validated macro recall and 6–9% FP on
three open models of different families and sizes** (Apertus-4B, Ministral-3B, Qwen3-4B). The
earlier per-model variation was largely a seed-construction artifact. Combined with the CE-08
Neuronpedia cross-validation (5/7 axes agree with independently-trained SAEs on Qwen), the
result is: *disposition is linearly and cheaply decodable from small-model hidden state,
forward-only, with a light per-model calibration — no SAE training required.*
